items.note: Use only for your own younger brother. Another person's younger brother is おとうとさん (otōtosan), which you also met in Lesson 9; Japanese keeps the humble and honorific family words separate.
items.reviewNote: Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 24: Work and Interests: I Work for an Apparel Maker (おとうと is formally taught later as part of the own-vs-others' family-vocabulary set)

items.note: ます-form stem かい (kai) + たいです (tai desu). The 〜たい ending conjugates like an い-adjective.

items.scene: talking about the time before an event
items.note: In Lesson 12, まえ (mae) meant only the spatial 'in front (of)'. Lesson 17 adds the time sense 'before', so の まえに now covers both 'in front of the station' and 'before the meeting'.
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 12: Asking about Places: What Is at Nikko? (matched on target) | Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 22: Forbidding Actions: Please Don’t Take Photos (borderline: まえ appears as a formal vocabulary entry later in its 〜まえ ('ago') sense; this entry's 'before; front' gloss may overlap)

items.note: Attaches to a noun: noun + の まえに (no mae ni), e.g. かいぎの まえに ("before the meeting"). For a verb instead, use the dictionary form + まえに (mae ni).
items.reviewNote: Written 〜の まえに in the source.

items.note: Dictionary-form verb + まえに (mae ni) = "before doing ..."; たべる (taberu) is the plain form of たべます (tabemasu).
ます-form stem いき (iki) + たいです (tai desu). Conjugates like an い-adjective.
Negative of いきたいです ("want to go"): たい → たくないです (taku nai desu).
Past of いきたいです ("want to go"): たい → たかったです (takatta desu).
Past negative of いきたいです ("want to go"): たい → たくなかったです (taku nakatta desu).
items.target: いきたくなかったです

items.note: With 〜たい (tai) the object may take が (ga) instead of を (o); ワインを のみたいです is equally correct.
items.reviewNote: GRAMMAR 1 NOTE — が-for-を substitution with 〜たい; source prints ワインを／が のみたいです。
items.target: ワインがのみたいです

items.note: ます-form stem たべ (tabe) + たいです (tai desu).
R2 (ru-verb). Plain form ねる (neru), as in ねる まえに ("before going to bed").

items.english: (I) want to eat some good sushi.
items.note: 〜たい (tai) states only the speaker's own wish, never someone else's.
items.target: おいしいおすしをたべたいです

items.english: Smith-san will send the materials before the meeting.
items.note: Pattern: person は + noun + の まえに (no mae ni) + verb — the action happens before that event.
items.target: スミスさんはかいぎのまえにしりょうをおくります

items.english: Smith-san does stretching exercises every day before going to bed.
items.note: Pattern: dictionary-form verb + まえに (mae ni) + main verb. ねる (neru) is the plain form of ねます (nemasu, "go to bed").
items.target: スミスさんはまいにちねるまえにストレッチをします

items.reviewNote: WORD POWER 'Hobbies' illustration ④; gloss supplied, not in the accompanying vocabulary box. | Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 15: Talking about Preferences: I Like Japanese Anime (matched on english)

items.note: Usually for a skill studied under a teacher (piano, karate); contrast べんきょうします (benkyō shimasu, "study") for academic study.
りょうり (ryōri, "cooking, cuisine") + を します.
R2 verb. あびます (abimasu) = "douse oneself with."

items.reviewNote: WORD POWER 'Verbs' illustration ⑤; gloss supplied, not in the accompanying vocabulary box. Formed as しょくじ (shokuji, "a meal") + を します. | Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 16: Making an Invitation: Shall We Go Together? (matched on target)

items.note: R2 verb, transitive: X を はじめます ('begin X'). Same はじめ- stem as はじめまして (hajimemashite, 'nice to meet you') from Lesson 1, but the two are unrelated in use.
Same verb as かく / かきます from Lesson 15, where it was glossed 'draw'. Japanese uses the one word for writing and for drawing, and both take を.
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 15: Talking about Preferences: I Like Japanese Anime (matched on target)

items.note: ます-form stem み (mi) + たいです (tai desu); from みます (mimasu, "see, watch").
ます-form stem あい (ai) + たいです (tai desu); from あいます (aimasu, "meet").
Negative wish: たべたいです → たべたくないです (tabetaku nai desu).
items.target: おすしをたべたくないです

items.reviewNote: Appears only in an Exercise II substitution cue (おんせんに いきます); not glossed in any vocabulary box this chapter. | Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 12: Asking about Places: What Is at Nikko? (matched on english)

items.note: Takes に for the place lived in: 〜に すみます. Not related to すみません (sumimasen, 'excuse me, I'm sorry') from Frequently Used Expressions, despite the close sound.
items.reviewNote: Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 24: Work and Interests: I Work for an Apparel Maker (borderline: the verb すむ is formally taught later as すんでいます (expressing a present state); reviewer should judge whether the bare すみます entry here overlaps)
Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 8: Doing Things (1): I’m Going to Eat Tempura (matched on english)

items.note: はなみ (hanami) = cherry-blossom viewing; commonly said with the honorific お as おはなみ (o-hanami).
items.reviewNote: Source shows the optional honorific: (お)はなみを します.

items.english: What kind of place do you want to live in in the future?
items.note: Asking about a future hope with 〜たいですか is acceptable even to someone of higher status; for everyday wishes it can sound too direct.
items.target: しょうらいどんなところにすみたいですか

items.english: I want to live near the sea.
items.scene: answering what kind of place you want to live in one day
items.target: うみのちかくにすみたいです

items.english: I want to study Japanese. Is there a good school near here?
items.target: にほんごをべんきょうしたいです。このちかくにいいがっこうがありますか

items.english: There is a party from 7:00 p.m.
items.note: 〜から (kara) here marks a start time. あります (arimasu) is used for events as well as objects.
items.target: ごご７じからパーティーがあります
items.ttsText: ごごしちじからパーティーがあります

items.english: I'll buy wine before the party.
items.note: noun + の まえに (no mae ni) + verb = "before (the event), do ..."
items.target: パーティーのまえにワインをかいます

items.note: Nearly homophonous with びょういん (byōin, "hospital"); this salon word has a long "yō."

items.english: Smith-san started studying Japanese before coming to Japan.
items.note: くる (kuru) is the plain form of きます (kimasu, "come"). Dictionary form + まえに (mae ni) is the same whether the main verb is present or past (here はじめました, "started").
items.target: スミスさんはにほんにくるまえににほんごのべんきょうをはじめました

items.reviewNote: Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 23: Explaining Actions: What Are You Doing Now? (チェック is listed as formally taught vocabulary in a later lesson)

items.note: Seen in てを あらいます (te o araimasu, "wash one's hands").
items.reviewNote: Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 21: Asking Permission: May I Have It? (て 'hand' is formally taught later as parts-of-the-body vocabulary)

items.note: Japanese speakers usually part with a phrase naming the next meeting rather than さようなら (sayōnara): じゃ、また + a day or time, e.g. じゃ、また すいようびに ('see you Wednesday'). Contrast またこんど (mata kondo) from Lesson 16, which defers vaguely to 'some other time' instead of naming one.
items.reviewNote: From the NOTES section example line.

items.scene: said just before starting to eat a meal
items.note: Set mealtime phrase with no literal English equivalent, roughly 'I gratefully receive.' Lesson 10 used the same word to gladly accept an offer ('yes, thank you'); here it is specifically what you say just before eating.
